claim: mGlu7 is a class C G protein-coupled receptor that modulates excitatory neurotransmitter release at the presynaptic active zone.
source: The metabotropic glutamate receptor 7 (mGlu7) is a class C G protein-coupled receptor that modulates excitatory neurotransmitter release at the presynaptic active zone.
evidence: This is stated in the Abstract as an established characteristic of mGlu7, supported by existing scientific knowledge.

claim: Nedd4 ubiquitin E3 ligase and β-arrestins regulate ubiquitination of mGlu7 in heterologous cells and rat neurons.
source: Here, we report that Nedd4 ubiquitin E3 ligase and β-arrestins regulate ubiquitination of mGlu7 in heterologous cells and rat neurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the Abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Upon agonist stimulation, β-arrestins recruit Nedd4 to mGlu7 and facilitate Nedd4-mediated ubiquitination of mGlu7.
source: Upon agonist stimulation, β-arrestins recruit Nedd4 to mGlu7 and facilitate Nedd4-mediated ubiquitination of mGlu7.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and related text.

claim: Nedd4 and β-arrestins regulate constitutive and agonist-induced endocytosis of mGlu7.
source: Nedd4 and β-arrestins regulate constitutive and agonist-induced endocytosis of mGlu7 and are required for mGlu7-dependent MAPK signaling in neurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 5.

claim: Nedd4 and β-arrestins are required for mGlu7-dependent MAPK signaling in neurons.
source: Nedd4 and β-arrestins regulate constitutive and agonist-induced endocytosis of mGlu7 and are required for mGlu7-dependent MAPK signaling in neurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 6.

claim: Nedd4-mediated ubiquitination results in the degradation of mGlu7 by both the ubiquitin-proteasome system and the lysosomal degradation pathway.
source: In addition, Nedd4-mediated ubiquitination results in the degradation of mGlu7 by both the ubiquitin-proteasome system and the lysosomal degradation pathway.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 7.

claim: mGlu7 is ubiquitinated in HEK 293 T cells when co-expressed with ubiquitin.
source: We observed diffuse high-molecular-weight mGlu7 immunoreactivities in the lane co-transfected with mGlu7 and ubiquitin, but not in the control lane transfected with either mGlu7 or ubiquitin, indicative of ubiquitinated mGlu7 signals (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A demonstrating ubiquitinated mGlu7 bands.

claim: Ubiquitinated mGlu7 is present mainly in dimeric and multimeric forms with apparent molecular weights larger than 200 kDa.
source: We found that the ubiquitinated mGlu7 bands are present mainly in dimeric and multimeric forms with apparent molecular weights larger than 200 kDa, whereas the monomeric form of mGlu7 (~100 kDa) is barely ubiquitinated (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A showing the molecular weight distribution of ubiquitinated mGlu7.

claim: The monomeric form of mGlu7 (~100 kDa) is barely ubiquitinated.
source: We found that the ubiquitinated mGlu7 bands are present mainly in dimeric and multimeric forms with apparent molecular weights larger than 200 kDa, whereas the monomeric form of mGlu7 (~100 kDa) is barely ubiquitinated (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: L-glutamate treatment increases mGlu7 ubiquitination approximately 2-fold within 10 min of agonist stimulation.
source: We were able to observe an approximately 2-fold increase in mGlu7 ubiquitination within 10 min of agonist stimulation, which was sustained up to 60 min.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B with quantification showing 1.77 ± 0.15 fold increase at 10 min.

claim: Agonist-induced mGlu7 ubiquitination is sustained up to 60 min.
source: We were able to observe an approximately 2-fold increase in mGlu7 ubiquitination within 10 min of agonist stimulation, which was sustained up to 60 min.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Total mGlu7 level is reduced after 30 min of agonist treatment, most likely due to receptor degradation.
source: Total mGlu7 level was reduced after 30 min most likely due to receptor degradation (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and represents an inference about the mechanism.

claim: L-AP4 treatment increases endogenous mGlu7 ubiquitination in cultured cortical neurons by approximately 2-fold.
source: We found that L-AP4 treatment increases endogenous mGlu7 ubiquitination in neurons by approximately 2-fold (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C with quantification showing 2.02 ± 0.23 fold increase.

claim: Surface-expressed mGlu7 undergoes agonist-induced ubiquitination.
source: We found that surface-expressed mGlu7 undergoes agonist-induced ubiquitination, whereas intracellular mGlu7 does not (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D using surface biotinylation and ubiquitin immunoprecipitation.

claim: Intracellular mGlu7 does not undergo agonist-induced ubiquitination.
source: We found that surface-expressed mGlu7 undergoes agonist-induced ubiquitination, whereas intracellular mGlu7 does not (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: mGlu7 ubiquitination occurs in combination with an agonist-induced endocytosis process.
source: This result suggests that mGlu7 ubiquitination occurs in combination with an agonist-induced endocytosis process.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that surface-expressed but not intracellular mGlu7 is ubiquitinated upon agonist stimulation.

claim: Nedd4 wild type co-expression results in robust ubiquitination of mGlu7 in HEK 293 T cells.
source: When Nedd4 wild type (WT) was co-expressed in HEK 293 T cells, we observed a robust ubiquitination of mGlu7, whereas Nedd4 C867S, a catalytically inactive form of Nedd4 (Blot et al., 2004; Kamynina et al., 2001), did not alter the ubiquitination level of mGlu7 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E with quantification showing 4.51 ± 0.52 fold increase.

claim: Nedd4 C867S, a catalytically inactive form of Nedd4, does not alter the ubiquitination level of mGlu7.
source: When Nedd4 wild type (WT) was co-expressed in HEK 293 T cells, we observed a robust ubiquitination of mGlu7, whereas Nedd4 C867S, a catalytically inactive form of Nedd4 (Blot et al., 2004; Kamynina et al., 2001), did not alter the ubiquitination level of mGlu7 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E and citations establishing C867S as catalytically inactive.

claim: Agonist L-AP4-induced mGlu7 ubiquitination is markedly reduced by Nedd4 knockdown in cultured cortical neurons.
source: Notably, agonist L-AP4-induced mGlu7 ubiquitination was markedly reduced by Nedd4 knockdown (Nedd4 KD), indicating that Nedd4 is required for agonist-induced mGlu7 ubiquitination (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Nedd4 is required for agonist-induced mGlu7 ubiquitination.
source: Notably, agonist L-AP4-induced mGlu7 ubiquitination was markedly reduced by Nedd4 knockdown (Nedd4 KD), indicating that Nedd4 is required for agonist-induced mGlu7 ubiquitination (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing reduced ubiquitination upon Nedd4 knockdown.

claim: Endogenous Nedd4 and mGlu7 show constitutive interaction in cultured cortical neurons.
source: We observed constitutive interaction between endogenous Nedd4 and mGlu7, and their interaction was markedly enhanced after treatment of L-AP4 for 5 min (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The interaction between endogenous Nedd4 and mGlu7 is markedly enhanced after treatment of L-AP4 for 5 min.
source: We observed constitutive interaction between endogenous Nedd4 and mGlu7, and their interaction was markedly enhanced after treatment of L-AP4 for 5 min (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G with quantification showing 2.36 ± 0.36 fold increase.

claim: Nedd4 is recruited to mGlu7 upon agonist-stimulation and plays a role as an E3 ubiquitin ligase for mGlu7 ubiquitination.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that Nedd4 is recruited to mGlu7 upon agonist-stimulation and plays a role as an E3 ubiquitin ligase for mGlu7 ubiquitination.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple experimental observations including interaction studies and ubiquitination assays.

claim: K63 ubiquitin is more efficiently conjugated to mGlu7 than K48 ubiquitin.
source: Although K63 ubiquitin was more efficiently conjugated to mGlu7 than K48 ubiquitin, there was no significant difference between K48- or K63-linked mGlu7 ubiquitination when their mGlu7 ubiquitination levels were normalized by the total expression levels of ubiquitin K48 or K63, respectively (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: There is no significant difference between K48- or K63-linked mGlu7 ubiquitination when normalized by total ubiquitin expression levels.
source: Although K63 ubiquitin was more efficiently conjugated to mGlu7 than K48 ubiquitin, there was no significant difference between K48- or K63-linked mGlu7 ubiquitination when their mGlu7 ubiquitination levels were normalized by the total expression levels of ubiquitin K48 or K63, respectively (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Ubiquitination of mGlu7 may regulate receptor endocytosis as well as degradation.
source: This result implicates that ubiquitination of mGlu7 may regulate receptor endocytosis as well as degradation.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation that both K48 and K63 ubiquitin linkages are present on mGlu7.

claim: mGlu7 contains eight lysine residues in the C-terminal tail.
source: We hypothesized that ubiquitin-conjugation of mGlu7 occurs in the eight lysine residues in the C-terminal tail (CT) of mGlu7 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is shown in the schematic diagram in Figure 2A.

claim: The level of ubiquitination was not reduced in mGlu7 deletion mutants including mGlu7 Δ857, which does not possess any lysine residues in its CT.
source: Unexpectedly, the level of ubiquitination was not reduced in any deletion mutants including mGlu7 Δ857, which does not possess any lysine residues in its CT (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: mGlu7 contains four lysine residues in the intracellular loop (iL) 2 and 3 domains.
source: We recognized four additional lysine residues present in the intracellular loop (iL) 2 and 3 domains (Figure 2A), and thus generated iL mutants such that all four lysine residues in iLs were individually replaced with arginine residues (mGlu7 iL 4K4R) by site-directed mutagenesis.
evidence: This is shown in the schematic diagram in Figure 2A.

claim: The mGlu7 CT 8K8R mutant is as efficiently ubiquitinated as mGlu7 WT after treatment of L-Glu for 5 min.
source: Consistent with the data using deletion mutants, the mGlu7 CT 8K8R mutant, in which all eight lysine residues in mGlu7 CT were mutated to arginines, was as efficiently ubiquitinated as mGlu7 WT after treatment of L-Glu for 5 min (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The efficiency of ubiquitination of mGlu7 iL 4K4R is similar to that of mGlu7 WT or CT 8K8R.
source: However, the efficiency of ubiquitination of mGlu7 iL 4K4R was also similar to that of mGlu7 WT or CT 8K8R (Figure 2C), suggesting that the lysines on iLs are not the only ubiquitination sites.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The lysines on iLs are not the only ubiquitination sites on mGlu7.
source: However, the efficiency of ubiquitination of mGlu7 iL 4K4R was also similar to that of mGlu7 WT or CT 8K8R (Figure 2C), suggesting that the lysines on iLs are not the only ubiquitination sites.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that iL mutation alone does not reduce ubiquitination.

claim: The ubiquitination of the mGlu7 12K12R mutant is almost completely abolished.
source: The ubiquitination of the mGlu7 12K12R mutant in which all twelve lysine residues were mutated to arginines was almost completely abolished (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C with quantification showing 0.11 ± 0.04 relative to WT.

claim: mGlu7 is ubiquitinated at lysine residues of both iLs and CT.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that mGlu7 is ubiquitinated at lysine residues of both iLs and CT.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mutagenesis data showing that both CT and iL lysines are required for ubiquitination.

claim: K688 and K689 mutations in the iL2 with mGlu7 Δ857 lead to marked reduction of mGlu7 ubiquitination.
source: We found that K688 and K689 mutations in the iL2 (iL K688/689R) with mGlu7 Δ857 lead to the marked reduction of mGlu7 ubiquitination to a similar level as iL 4K4R with mGlu7 Δ857, suggesting the K688 and K689 residues are ubiquitinated residues in the iL domains of mGlu7 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: K688 and K689 residues are ubiquitinated residues in the iL domains of mGlu7.
source: We found that K688 and K689 mutations in the iL2 (iL K688/689R) with mGlu7 Δ857 lead to the marked reduction of mGlu7 ubiquitination to a similar level as iL 4K4R with mGlu7 Δ857, suggesting the K688 and K689 residues are ubiquitinated residues in the iL domains of mGlu7 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the mutagenesis data.

claim: The two lysine residues K688 and K689 in iL2 and all eight lysine residues in CT are the target ubiquitination residues of mGlu7.
source: However, in spite of further mutagenesis studies we were not able to identify dominant ubiquitination sites among eight mGlu7 CT resides (data not shown), suggesting that the two lysine residues K688 and K689 in iL2 and all eight lysine residues in CT are the target ubiquitination residues of mGlu7.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on mutagenesis studies.

claim: β-arrestin 2 plays a role as an adaptor for β2AR ubiquitination by recruiting Nedd4 E3 ligase upon agonist stimulation.
source: Previous studies have shown that β-arrestin 2 plays a role as an adaptor for β2AR ubiquitination by recruiting Nedd4 E3 ligase upon agonist stimulation (Shenoy et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: β-arrestins are involved in the desensitization, endocytosis, and intracellular signaling of Group I mGlu receptors.
source: It has also been reported that β-arrestins are involved in the desensitization, endocytosis, and intracellular signaling of Group I mGlu receptors (reviewed in Suh et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: β-arrestin 1 robustly binds to mGlu7 as well as β2AR.
source: As evident from Figure 3—figure supplement 1, β-arrestin 1 robustly binds to mGlu7 as well as β2AR, whereas the binding affinity of β-arrestin 2 to mGlu7 appears to be lower (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The binding affinity of β-arrestin 2 to mGlu7 appears to be lower than β-arrestin 1.
source: As evident from Figure 3—figure supplement 1, β-arrestin 1 robustly binds to mGlu7 as well as β2AR, whereas the binding affinity of β-arrestin 2 to mGlu7 appears to be lower (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: β-arrestins and Nedd4 bind constitutively to mGlu7 before stimulation with agonist L-Glu.
source: We observed that β-arrestins and Nedd4 bind constitutively to mGlu7 before stimulation with agonist L-Glu (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: Agonist stimulation rapidly increases binding of β-arrestin 1 to mGlu7 within 5 min by approximately 1.8 fold relative to basal binding levels.
source: Of particular interest, agonist stimulation rapidly increased binding of β-arrestin 1 to mGlu7 within 5 min by approximately 1.8 fold relative to basal binding levels (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3A and 3C with quantification showing 1.79 ± 0.31 fold increase.

claim: β-arrestin 1 interaction with mGlu7 is sustained for 15 min and decreases to basal levels after 30 min.
source: This interaction was sustained for 15 min and decreased to basal levels after 30 min (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3A and 3C.

claim: Binding of Nedd4 to mGlu7 is elevated after 5 min of agonist stimulation when β-arrestin 1 is co-expressed.
source: Binding of Nedd4 to mGlu7 was also elevated after 5 min of agonist stimulation when β-arrestin 1 was co-expressed (Figure 3A,D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3A and 3D with quantification showing 2.36 ± 0.57 fold increase.

claim: After 60 min of agonist treatment, binding of β-arrestin 1 or Nedd4 to mGlu7 is reduced, probably due to the degradation of the receptor.
source: After 60 min of agonist treatment, binding of β-arrestin 1 or Nedd4 to mGlu7 was reduced, probably due to the degradation of the receptor (Figure 3A,C,D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3A, 3C, and 3D, with an inference about the mechanism.

claim: Binding of β-arrestin 2 to mGlu7 exhibits a smaller degree of increase by 1.2 fold at 5 min after agonist treatment.
source: Binding of β-arrestin 2 to mGlu7 exhibited a smaller degree of increase by 1.2 fold at 5 min after agonist treatment (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3B and 3C with quantification showing 1.36 ± 0.10 fold increase.

claim: Nedd4 binding to mGlu7 is increased at 5 min of agonist stimulation when β-arrestin 2 is co-expressed.
source: Nedd4 binding to mGlu7 was also increased at 5 min of agonist stimulation when β-arrestin 2 was co-expressed (Figure 3B,D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3B and 3D with quantification showing 2.20 ± 0.36 fold increase.

claim: β-arrestin 1 and Nedd4 are rapidly associated within 1 min after mGlu7 agonist stimulation.
source: We found that β-arrestin 1 and Nedd4 are rapidly associated within 1 min and their interaction continued more than 10 min after mGlu7 agonist stimulation (Figure 3E,F), suggesting that Nedd4 is recruited to the activated mGlu7 by β-arrestin 1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3E and 3F with quantification showing 1.67 ± 0.12 fold increase at 1 min.

claim: The interaction between β-arrestin 1 and Nedd4 continues more than 10 min after mGlu7 agonist stimulation.
source: We found that β-arrestin 1 and Nedd4 are rapidly associated within 1 min and their interaction continued more than 10 min after mGlu7 agonist stimulation (Figure 3E,F), suggesting that Nedd4 is recruited to the activated mGlu7 by β-arrestin 1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3E and 3F.

claim: Nedd4 is recruited to the activated mGlu7 by β-arrestin 1.
source: We found that β-arrestin 1 and Nedd4 are rapidly associated within 1 min and their interaction continued more than 10 min after mGlu7 agonist stimulation (Figure 3E,F), suggesting that Nedd4 is recruited to the activated mGlu7 by β-arrestin 1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the time course of interactions observed.

claim: Endogenous β-arrestin 1, Nedd4, and mGlu7 are present in the same complex in cortical neurons.
source: To investigate if endogenous mGlu7, Nedd4, and β-arrestin 1 are present at the same complex, we performed co-immunoprecipitation assay using anti-β-arrestin 1 antibody in cortical neurons. We have found that three proteins are present in the same complex and that their binding affinity is increased by agonist treatment (Figure 3G,H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3G and 3H.

claim: The binding affinity of endogenous β-arrestin 1, Nedd4, and mGlu7 is increased by agonist treatment.
source: We have found that three proteins are present in the same complex and that their binding affinity is increased by agonist treatment (Figure 3G,H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3G and 3H with quantification showing 1.56 ± 0.19 fold increase for mGlu7 and 1.46 ± 0.13 fold increase for Nedd4.

claim: Binding affinity of Nedd4 or β-arrestin 1 to different mGlu7 ubiquitination site mutants is not altered in neurons.
source: However, binding affinity of Nedd4 or β-arrestin 1 to different mGlu7 ubiquitination site mutants was not altered in neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Either β-arrestin 1 or 2 knockdown abolishes an increase in agonist-induced binding of Nedd4 to mGlu7 in HEK 293 T cells.
source: We found that either β-arrestin 1 (β-arr1 KD) or 2 knockdown (β-arr2 KD) abolished an increase in agonist-induced binding of Nedd4 to mGlu7 (Figure 3I,J),
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3I and 3J.

claim: When both β-arrestin 1 and 2 are simultaneously knocked down in neurons, there is a significant reduction of agonist-induced Nedd4 recruitment to mGlu7.
source: However, when both β-arrestin 1 and 2 were simultaneously knocked down, we observed a significant reduction of agonist-induced Nedd4 recruitment to mGlu7 (Figure 3K,L, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3K, 3L, and Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: β-arrestin 1 and 2 may compensate for the function of each other in neurons due to their high expression but not in heterologous cells due to their stoichiometrically low expression.
source: Endogenously expressed levels of β-arrestins are high in the brain, but relatively low in HEK 293 T cells because only mGlu7 and Nedd4 were exogenously overexpressed in HEK 293 T cells (Attramadal et al., 1992; Barlic et al., 1999). Therefore, we hypothesize that β-arrestin 1 and 2 may compensate for the function of each other in neurons due to their high expression but not in heterologous cells due to their stoichiometrically low expression.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on known expression levels and experimental observations, supported by citations.

claim: Agonist-induced recruitment of Nedd4 to mGlu7 is mediated by β-arrestins.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that agonist-induced recruitment of Nedd4 to mGlu7 is mediated by β-arrestins.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple experimental observations showing β-arrestin dependence.

claim: Agonist-induced mGlu7 ubiquitination levels are significantly reduced by either β-arrestin 1 or 2 KD in cultured cortical neurons.
source: We found that agonist-induced mGlu7 ubiquitination levels were significantly reduced by either β-arrestin 1 or 2 KD, and further decreased by double KD of β-arrestin 1 and 2 compared with the control non-related target knockdown (Ctl KD) in cultured cortical neurons (Figure 3M,N, Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3M, 3N, and Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Agonist-induced mGlu7 ubiquitination is further decreased by double KD of β-arrestin 1 and 2 compared with control KD.
source: We found that agonist-induced mGlu7 ubiquitination levels were significantly reduced by either β-arrestin 1 or 2 KD, and further decreased by double KD of β-arrestin 1 and 2 compared with the control non-related target knockdown (Ctl KD) in cultured cortical neurons (Figure 3M,N, Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3M, 3N, and Figure 3—figure supplement 4 with quantification showing 0.50 ± 0.03 for double KD.

claim: β-arrestins recruit Nedd4 to mGlu7 and facilitate mGlu7 ubiquitination upon agonist stimulation.
source: These results indicate that β-arrestins recruit Nedd4 to mGlu7 and facilitate mGlu7 ubiquitination upon agonist stimulation, and agonist-induced mGlu7 ubiquitination is regulated by the recruitment of β-arrestins.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple experimental observations.

claim: Agonist-induced mGlu7 ubiquitination is regulated by the recruitment of β-arrestins.
source: These results indicate that β-arrestins recruit Nedd4 to mGlu7 and facilitate mGlu7 ubiquitination upon agonist stimulation, and agonist-induced mGlu7 ubiquitination is regulated by the recruitment of β-arrestins.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple experimental observations.

claim: Both Nedd4 and β-arrestin 1 bind to the CTs of mGlu7a as well as mGlu7b.
source: We found that both Nedd4 and β-arrestin 1 bind to the CTs of mGlu7a as well as mGlu7b (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A using GST pull-down assays.

claim: Nedd4 interacts with the iL2 domain and to a lesser extent with the iL1 domain of mGlu7.
source: Additionally, Nedd4 interacted with the iL2 domain and to a lesser extent with the iL1 domain of mGlu7.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: β-arrestin 1 shows strong interaction with the iL2 domain of mGlu7.
source: While protein phosphatase 1γ1 (PP1γ1) interacted only with mGlu7b CT as previously shown (Suh et al., 2013), β-arrestin 1 showed strong interaction with the iL2 domain of mGlu7 (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and citation to previous work.

claim: Purified Nedd4 protein directly binds to mGlu7 CT and iL2 domains.
source: We performed in vitro binding assays and found that purified Nedd4 protein directly binds to mGlu7 CT and iL2 domains immobilized on Glutathione-Sepharose beads (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B using purified recombinant proteins.

claim: Both β-arrestin 1 and β-arrestin 2 purified proteins directly interact with mGlu7 CTs and iL2.
source: Both β-arrestin 1 and β-arrestin 2 purified proteins also directly interacted with mGlu7 CTs and iL2 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B using purified recombinant proteins.

claim: Nedd4 ΔHECT mutant does not interact with mGlu7.
source: We performed co-immunoprecipitation assay with myc-mGlu7, and found that Nedd4 ΔHECT mutant does not interact with mGlu7, indicating the Nedd4 HECT domain is responsible for interaction with mGlu7 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The Nedd4 HECT domain is responsible for interaction with mGlu7.
source: We performed co-immunoprecipitation assay with myc-mGlu7, and found that Nedd4 ΔHECT mutant does not interact with mGlu7, indicating the Nedd4 HECT domain is responsible for interaction with mGlu7 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the deletion mutant data.

claim: Treatment of cultured cortical neurons with MLN7243 results in increased surface expression of endogenous mGlu7.
source: When we treated cultured cortical neurons with MLN7243, we found surface expression of endogenous mGlu7 is increased while mGlu7 ubiquitination is reduced (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Treatment of cultured cortical neurons with MLN7243 results in reduced mGlu7 ubiquitination.
source: When we treated cultured cortical neurons with MLN7243, we found surface expression of endogenous mGlu7 is increased while mGlu7 ubiquitination is reduced (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nedd4 WT markedly increases mGlu7 endocytosis in cultured hippocampal neurons.
source: We observed a marked increase in mGlu7 endocytosis by Nedd4 WT, but not by Nedd4 C867S (Figure 5A,B; Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5A, 5B, and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A with quantification showing 1.23 ± 0.04 fold increase.

claim: Nedd4 C867S does not increase mGlu7 endocytosis in cultured hippocampal neurons.
source: We observed a marked increase in mGlu7 endocytosis by Nedd4 WT, but not by Nedd4 C867S (Figure 5A,B; Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5A, 5B, and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Agonist-induced endocytosis of mGlu7 is impaired by co-expression of Nedd4 shRNA in hippocampal neurons.
source: We also found that agonist-induced endocytosis of mGlu7 was impaired by co-expression of Nedd4 shRNA (Nedd4 KD) compared with control shRNA (Ctl KD) in hippocampal neurons (Figure 5C,D; Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5C, 5D, and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Agonist-induced endocytosis of mGlu7 is regulated by Nedd4-mediated ubiquitin modification of receptor.
source: These results indicate that agonist-induced endocytosis of mGlu7 is regulated by Nedd4-mediated ubiquitin modification of receptor.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the Nedd4 overexpression and knockdown experiments.

claim: Co-expression of β-arrestin 1 or 2 with mGlu7 results in a profound increase in internalization of mGlu7 in cultured hippocampal neurons.
source: When β-arrestin 1 or 2 was co-expressed with mGlu7, we found a profound increase in internalization of mGlu7 by either β-arrestin 1 or 2 in cultured hippocampal neurons (Figure 5E,F; Figure 5—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5E, 5F, and Figure 5—figure supplement 2C with quantification showing 1.26 ± 0.07 for β-arr1 and 1.30 ± 0.07 for β-arr2.

claim: Agonist-induced mGlu7 ubiquitination by the Nedd4-β-arrestin complex promotes receptor endocytosis in hippocampal neurons.
source: These results indicate agonist-induced mGlu7 ubiquitination by the Nedd4-β-arrestin complex promotes receptor endocytosis in hippocampal neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined effects of Nedd4 and β-arrestins on endocytosis.

claim: ERK1/2 phosphorylation significantly increases after 5 min treatment with L-AP4 in control KD or β-arr1 KD neurons.
source: We observed that ERK1/2 phosphorylation significantly increased after 5 min treatment with L-AP4 in Ctl KD or β-arr1 KD neurons, whereas β-arr2 KD or Nedd4 KD did not induce agonist-induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation (Figure 6A,B), indicating the necessity for β-arrestin 2 and Nedd4 in mGlu7-mediated ERK signaling.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: β-arr2 KD or Nedd4 KD does not induce agonist-induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation.
source: We observed that ERK1/2 phosphorylation significantly increased after 5 min treatment with L-AP4 in Ctl KD or β-arr1 KD neurons, whereas β-arr2 KD or Nedd4 KD did not induce agonist-induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation (Figure 6A,B), indicating the necessity for β-arrestin 2 and Nedd4 in mGlu7-mediated ERK signaling.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: β-arrestin 2 and Nedd4 are necessary for mGlu7-mediated ERK signaling.
source: We observed that ERK1/2 phosphorylation significantly increased after 5 min treatment with L-AP4 in Ctl KD or β-arr1 KD neurons, whereas β-arr2 KD or Nedd4 KD did not induce agonist-induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation (Figure 6A,B), indicating the necessity for β-arrestin 2 and Nedd4 in mGlu7-mediated ERK signaling.
evidence: This is an inference based on the knockdown experiments.

claim: β-arr2 KD impairs agonist-induced c-Jun N-terminal kinases (JNKs) activation.
source: We observed a similar impairment of agonist-induced c-Jun N-terminal kinases (JNKs) activation in β-arr2 KD neurons.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6A and 6C.

claim: β-arr1 KD or Nedd4 KD shows little effect on mGlu7-mediated JNK signaling.
source: Either β-arr1 KD or Nedd4 KD showed little effect on mGlu7-mediated JNK signaling (Figure 6A,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6A and 6C.

claim: mGlu7-dependent ERK signaling is regulated by β-arrestin 2 and depends on Nedd4-mediated ubiquitination.
source: These results suggest that mGlu7-dependent ERK signaling is regulated by β-arrestin 2 and depends on Nedd4-mediated ubiquitination, whereas JNK signaling is independent of Nedd4-mediated ubiquitination in neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the differential effects of β-arrestin 2 and Nedd4 knockdown on ERK versus JNK signaling.

claim: JNK signaling is independent of Nedd4-mediated ubiquitination in neurons.
source: These results suggest that mGlu7-dependent ERK signaling is regulated by β-arrestin 2 and depends on Nedd4-mediated ubiquitination, whereas JNK signaling is independent of Nedd4-mediated ubiquitination in neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that Nedd4 KD does not affect JNK signaling.

claim: Total expression of mGlu7 is reduced when Nedd4 is co-expressed with mGlu7 in HEK 293 T cells.
source: As is evident in Figure 7A, total expression of mGlu7 was reduced when Nedd4 was co-expressed with mGlu7.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Co-expression of Nedd4 C867S has little effect on total expression of mGlu7.
source: However, co-expression of Nedd4 C867S had little effect on total expression of mGlu7 (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Total expression level of mGlu7 is reduced by L-Glu treatment for 60 min.
source: The total expression level of mGlu7 was reduced by L-Glu treatment for 60 min, which was blocked by co-expression of Nedd4 C867S (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: L-Glu-induced mGlu7 degradation is blocked by co-expression of Nedd4 C867S.
source: The total expression level of mGlu7 was reduced by L-Glu treatment for 60 min, which was blocked by co-expression of Nedd4 C867S (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The surface stability of mGlu7 is determined by Nedd4-mediated ubiquitin modification of mGlu7.
source: These results indicate that the surface stability of mGlu7 is determined by Nedd4-mediated ubiquitin modification of mGlu7.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the effects of Nedd4 WT versus C867S on mGlu7 expression.

claim: Agonist-induced mGlu7 degradation is significantly blocked by leupeptin treatment.
source: We found that agonist-induced mGlu7 degradation was significantly blocked by leupeptin treatment (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 7C and 7D with quantification showing 1.23 ± 0.18 for Leu + L-Glu.

claim: Ubiquitination regulates the intracellular sorting of mGlu7 into early and late endosomes, and subsequent degradation in lysosomes.
source: This result indicates that ubiquitination regulates the intracellular sorting of mGlu7 into early and late endosomes, and subsequent degradation in lysosomes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the effect of lysosome inhibitor on mGlu7 degradation.

claim: MG132 inhibits agonist-induced mGlu7 degradation.
source: Furthermore, we were able to observe that MG132 also inhibits agonist-induced mGlu7 degradation (Figure 7C,D), implying that ubiquitin-proteasome system is also involved in the control of mGlu7 protein homeostasis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 7C and 7D with quantification showing 1.14 ± 0.15 for MG132 + L-Glu.

claim: Ubiquitin-proteasome system is involved in the control of mGlu7 protein homeostasis.
source: Furthermore, we were able to observe that MG132 also inhibits agonist-induced mGlu7 degradation (Figure 7C,D), implying that ubiquitin-proteasome system is also involved in the control of mGlu7 protein homeostasis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the effect of proteasome inhibitor on mGlu7 degradation.

claim: Nedd4 WT significantly reduces mGlu7 expression in cultured cortical neurons.
source: We found that Nedd4 WT significantly reduced mGlu7 expression in neurons, whereas Nedd4 C867S did not.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 7E and 7F with quantification showing 0.81 ± 0.09 for Nedd4 WT.

claim: Nedd4 C867S does not reduce mGlu7 expression in cultured cortical neurons.
source: We found that Nedd4 WT significantly reduced mGlu7 expression in neurons, whereas Nedd4 C867S did not.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 7E and 7F.

claim: Nedd4 WT-mediated mGlu7 degradation is blocked by MG132 or leupeptin in neurons.
source: In addition, Nedd4 WT-mediated mGlu7 degradation was blocked by MG132 or leupeptin (Figure 7E,F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 7E and 7F with quantification showing 1.06 ± 0.13 for Nedd4 WT + MG132 and 1.00 ± 0.13 for Nedd4 WT + Leu.

claim: Nedd4-mediated ubiquitination is required for mGlu7 degradation, which is accomplished through the proteasomal and lysosomal degradation pathways in neurons.
source: Thus, Nedd4-mediated ubiquitination is required for mGlu7 degradation, which is accomplished through the proteasomal and lysosomal degradation pathways in neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined effects of Nedd4 and proteasome/lysosome inhibitors.

claim: mGlu7 is only activated under conditions of sustained synaptic activity due to its low affinity for glutamate.
source: mGlu7 is only activated under conditions of sustained synaptic activity due to its low affinity for glutamate, thereby acting as an auto-inhibitory receptor (Niswender and Conn, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Agonist-induced mGlu7 endocytosis underlies a presynaptic form of long-term depression (LTD).
source: In particular, agonist-induced mGlu7 endocytosis underlies a presynaptic form of long-term depression (LTD) and regulates a metaplastic switch at the mossy fiber-CA3 stratum lucidum interneuron (MF-SLIN) synapses.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Introduction.

claim: At naive MF-SLIN synapses, high frequency stimulation (HFS) or agonist L-AP4 treatment triggers presynaptic LTD by mGlu7 activation.
source: At naive MF-SLIN synapses, high frequency stimulation (HFS) or agonist L-AP4 treatment triggers presynaptic LTD by mGlu7 activation. Following L-AP4-induced internalization of mGlu7, the same HFS produces presynaptic LTP, which requires the activation of the adenylate cyclase-cAMP-PKA pathway and subsequent action of RIM1α (Pelkey et al., 2005; Pelkey et al., 2008; Suh et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Following L-AP4-induced internalization of mGlu7, HFS produces presynaptic LTP, which requires the activation of the adenylate cyclase-cAMP-PKA pathway and subsequent action of RIM1α.
source: Following L-AP4-induced internalization of mGlu7, the same HFS produces presynaptic LTP, which requires the activation of the adenylate cyclase-cAMP-PKA pathway and subsequent action of RIM1α (Pelkey et al., 2005; Pelkey et al., 2008; Suh et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Ubiquitination of target substrates is achieved by the covalent attachment of ubiquitin to lysine residues of substrates through a three-enzyme cascade catalyzed by E1, E2, and E3 enzymes.
source: Ubiquitination of target substrates is achieved by the covalent attachment of ubiquitin to lysine residues of substrates through a three-enzyme cascade catalyzed by E1 (ubiquitin activating), E2 (ubiquitin conjugating), and E3 (ubiquitin ligase) enzymes.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the ubiquitination process.

claim: The E3 ubiquitin ligase catalyzes the transfer of the ubiquitin moiety from E2 enzymes to the target substrates and plays a key role in determining the substrate specificity of ubiquitination.
source: The E3 ubiquitin ligase catalyzes the transfer of the ubiquitin moiety from E2 enzymes to the target substrates and plays a key role in determining the substrate specificity of ubiquitination.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about E3 ligase function.

claim: Nedd4 E3 ligase has been well characterized in its regulation of the turnover and trafficking of ion channels and GPCRs present in neurons.
source: Among the several hundred E3 ubiquitin ligases in mammals, Nedd4 (Neural precursor cell-expressed developmentally down-regulated 4) (also known as Nedd4-1) E3 ligase, which belongs to the HECT (Homologous to E6-associated protein Carboxyl Terminus) domain-containing family (Rotin and Kumar, 2009), has been well characterized in its regulation of the turnover and trafficking of ion channels and GPCRs present in neurons such as voltage-gated sodium channels, calcium channels, GluA1 AMPA receptor, GluN2D-containing NMDA receptor, Na+/H+ exchanger 1, and β2-adrenergic receptor (β2AR) (Boase and Kumar, 2015; Gautam et al., 2013; Han et al., 2013; Lin et al., 2011; Rougier et al., 2011; Schwarz et al., 2010; Shenoy and Lefkowitz, 2011; Shenoy et al., 2008; Simonin and Fuster, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: β-arrestin 1 and β-arrestin 2 are cytosolic adaptor proteins involved in the regulation of GPCR desensitization, trafficking, and signaling.
source: β-arrestin 1 (also known as arrestin 2) and β-arrestin 2 (also known as arrestin 3) are cytosolic adaptor proteins involved in the regulation of GPCR desensitization, trafficking, and signaling (DeWire et al., 2007; Luttrell and Gesty-Palmer, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Following agonist stimulation, β-arrestins are rapidly recruited to phosphorylated activated β2AR at the plasma membrane.
source: Following agonist stimulation, β-arrestins are rapidly recruited to phosphorylated activated β2AR at the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is established knowledge about β-arrestin function with β2AR.

claim: β-arrestins typically terminate the interaction of receptors with G-proteins.
source: β-arrestins typically terminate the interaction of receptors with G-proteins, however recent studies indicate that β-arrestins trigger the ubiquitination of receptors and give rise to distinct signaling pathways independently of G-proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge about β-arrestin function.

claim: β-arrestins trigger the ubiquitination of receptors and give rise to distinct signaling pathways independently of G-proteins.
source: β-arrestins typically terminate the interaction of receptors with G-proteins, however recent studies indicate that β-arrestins trigger the ubiquitination of receptors and give rise to distinct signaling pathways independently of G-proteins.
evidence: This is supported by recent studies as indicated in the text.

claim: Upon agonist stimulation of β2AR, β-arrestins act as adaptors to initiate recruitment of E3 ubiquitin ligases such as Nedd4 or Mdm2 as well as the clathrin-AP2 adaptor complex.
source: Upon agonist stimulation of β2AR, β-arrestins act as adaptors to initiate recruitment of E3 ubiquitin ligases such as Nedd4 or Mdm2 as well as the clathrin-AP2 adaptor complex, thereby promoting endocytosis of β-arrestin-bound receptors (Jean-Charles et al., 2016; Shenoy et al., 2001; Shenoy et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Class A receptors exhibit a transient interaction with β-arrestins, undergo recycling pathways, and induce weak ERK signaling.
source: While class A receptors (e.g. β2AR) exhibit a transient interaction with β-arrestins, undergo recycling pathways, and induce weak extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) signaling, class B receptors such as Angiotensin II type 1a receptor (AT1aR) and vasopressin V2 receptor (V2R) display more robust interaction with β-arrestins that gives rise to the receptor-G protein-β-arrestin super-complex in the endosomes, induce robust and sustained ERK activity, and are targeted for degradation (Eichel et al., 2018; Ranjan et al., 2017; Shenoy and Lefkowitz, 2011; Thomsen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Class B receptors display more robust interaction with β-arrestins that gives rise to the receptor-G protein-β-arrestin super-complex in the endosomes, induce robust and sustained ERK activity, and are targeted for degradation.
source: While class A receptors (e.g. β2AR) exhibit a transient interaction with β-arrestins, undergo recycling pathways, and induce weak extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) signaling, class B receptors such as Angiotensin II type 1a receptor (AT1aR) and vasopressin V2 receptor (V2R) display more robust interaction with β-arrestins that gives rise to the receptor-G protein-β-arrestin super-complex in the endosomes, induce robust and sustained ERK activity, and are targeted for degradation (Eichel et al., 2018; Ranjan et al., 2017; Shenoy and Lefkowitz, 2011; Thomsen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The roles of β-arrestins in regulating trafficking and function of class C GPCRs remain poorly understood.
source: However, the roles of β-arrestins in regulating trafficking and function of class C GPCRs remain poorly understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Nedd4 and β-arrestins are constitutively associated with mGlu7.
source: We show that Nedd4 and β-arrestins are constitutively associated with mGlu7 and recruited to mGlu7 by agonist stimulation, revealing the essential roles of β-arrestin as an adaptor that recruits Nedd4 to mediate ubiquitination and endocytosis of mGlu7.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Introduction and supported by experimental data.

claim: β-arrestin acts as an adaptor that recruits Nedd4 to mediate ubiquitination and endocytosis of mGlu7.
source: We show that Nedd4 and β-arrestins are constitutively associated with mGlu7 and recruited to mGlu7 by agonist stimulation, revealing the essential roles of β-arrestin as an adaptor that recruits Nedd4 to mediate ubiquitination and endocytosis of mGlu7.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Introduction and supported by experimental data.

claim: β-arrestin 2 and Nedd4 regulate mGlu7-mediated mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling.
source: In addition, we demonstrate that β-arrestin 2 and Nedd4 regulate mGlu7-mediated mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling, and Nedd4 is required for agonist-induced receptor degradation via both the proteasomal and the lysosomal pathways.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Introduction and supported by experimental data.

claim: Nedd4 is required for agonist-induced receptor degradation via both the proteasomal and the lysosomal pathways.
source: In addition, we demonstrate that β-arrestin 2 and Nedd4 regulate mGlu7-mediated mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling, and Nedd4 is required for agonist-induced receptor degradation via both the proteasomal and the lysosomal pathways.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Introduction and supported by experimental data.

claim: The formation of K48-linked polyubiquitin chain typically directs protein substrates to the proteasomal degradation.
source: It is well known that among seven lysine residues of the ubiquitin protein, the formation of K48- or K63-linked polyubiquitin chain typically directs protein substrates to the proteasomal degradation or endocytic trafficking, respectively (Alonso and Friedman, 2013; Dores and Trejo, 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The formation of K63-linked polyubiquitin chain typically directs protein substrates to endocytic trafficking.
source: It is well known that among seven lysine residues of the ubiquitin protein, the formation of K48- or K63-linked polyubiquitin chain typically directs protein substrates to the proteasomal degradation or endocytic trafficking, respectively (Alonso and Friedman, 2013; Dores and Trejo, 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Siah-1A is the first identified E3 ubiquitin ligase for Group 1 mGlu receptors.
source: Siah-1A (seven in absentia homolog-1A) is the first identified E3 ubiquitin ligase for Group 1 mGlu receptors (Moriyoshi et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Siah-1A directly binds to Group 1 mGlu receptors and mediates receptor ubiquitination, resulting in receptor degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.
source: Siah-1A directly binds to Group 1 mGlu receptors and mediates receptor ubiquitination, resulting in receptor degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Siah-1A regulates agonist-induced endocytosis of mGlu5 by displacing calmodulin binding, and promotes the lysosomal degradation of mGlu5.
source: Siah-1A also regulates agonist-induced endocytosis of mGlu5 by displacing calmodulin binding, and promotes the lysosomal degradation of mGlu5 (Gulia et al., 2017; Ishikawa et al., 1999; Ko et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: mGlu7 does not possess the PPxY motif, a canonical Nedd4 binding motif.
source: Although mGlu7 does not possess the PPxY motif, a canonical Nedd4 binding motif, Nedd4 directly binds to the iL2 and CT domains of mGlu7 by the HECT domain of Nedd4.
evidence: This is an observation about the sequence of mGlu7.

claim: Endogenous mGlu7 ubiquitination induced by agonist stimulation is less prominent in neurons compared to exogenous expression in HEK 293 T cells.
source: We observed a marked induction of mGlu7 ubiquitination when exogenous ubiquitin was co-expressed with mGlu7 in HEK 293 T cells. In contrast, endogenous mGlu7 ubiquitination induced by agonist stimulation was less prominent in neurons (Figure 1C,F).
evidence: This is an observation comparing results between different experimental systems.

claim: Only the surface-expressed fraction of mGlu7 can be ubiquitinated directly from agonist stimulation.
source: This result likely occurs because only the surface-expressed fraction of mGlu7 can be ubiquitinated directly from agonist stimulation.
evidence: This is an inference to explain the observation of less prominent endogenous ubiquitination.

claim: Other E3 ligases than Nedd4 may play a role in mGlu7 ubiquitination in neurons.
source: Of note, we observed some remaining levels of mGlu7 ubiquitination despite the loss of Nedd4 in Figure 1F. This result suggests that other E3 ligases than Nedd4 may play a role in mGlu7 ubiquitination in neurons.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation of residual ubiquitination after Nedd4 knockdown.

claim: A serine/threonine rich domain on mGlu7 CT (868-TAATMSSRLS-877) is compatible with the phosphorylation code for arrestin binding.
source: A serine/threonine rich domain on mGlu7 CT (868-TAATMSSRLS-877) is compatible with this phosphorylation code for arrestin binding, and is therefore a candidate β-arrestin-interacting domain.
evidence: This is an inference based on sequence analysis and comparison to known arrestin binding motifs.

claim: The iL2 domain of GPCRs contributes to association with β-arrestin by providing a partial core contact site for both Gα and β-arrestin.
source: In addition, the iL2 domain of GPCRs has been shown to contribute to association with β-arrestin by providing a partial core contact site for both Gα and β-arrestin (Hilger et al., 2018; Latorraca et al., 2018; Ranjan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The iL2 domain of mGlu receptors including mGlu8 determines G-protein coupling selectivity.
source: It was shown that the iL2 domain of mGlu receptors including mGlu8 determines G-protein coupling selectivity (Francesconi and Duvoisin, 1998; Gomeza et al., 1996; Havlickova et al., 2003; Pin et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The iL2 domain of mGlu1 is a site for GRK2 binding and GRK2-mediated signaling.
source: Furthermore, in addition to the CT domain, the iL2 domain of mGlu1 is a site for GRK2 binding and GRK2-mediated signaling (Dhami et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Additional binding of β-arrestin-Nedd4 complex to mGlu7 iL2 may sterically hinder G-protein binding and provide a platform for a receptor core for fully-engaged binding of β-arrestin to mGlu7.
source: Accordingly, additional binding of β-arrestin-Nedd4 complex to mGlu7 iL2 may sterically hinder G-protein binding and provide a platform for a receptor core for fully-engaged binding of β-arrestin to mGlu7.
evidence: This is speculation about the functional consequences of iL2 binding.

claim: mGlu7 ubiquitination per se is not a prerequisite for the complex formation with β-arrestins and Nedd4.
source: Although we observed β-arrestins and Nedd4 bind constitutively to mGlu7, binding affinity of Nedd4 or β-arrestin 1 to mGlu7 is not affected by ubiquitination site mutations in neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 2). This result suggests that mGlu7 ubiquitination per se is not a prerequisite for the complex formation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that ubiquitination site mutants still bind β-arrestins and Nedd4.

claim: β-arrestin 1 and β-arrestin 2 are functionally redundant due to the high degree of sequence and structural similarity.
source: It has been expected that β-arrestin 1 and β-arrestin 2 are functionally redundant due to the high degree of sequence and structural similarity, however recent studies have suggested their partially distinct functional roles (Srivastava et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about expectations in the field, supported by citation.

claim: Recent studies have suggested β-arrestin 1 and β-arrestin 2 have partially distinct functional roles.
source: It has been expected that β-arrestin 1 and β-arrestin 2 are functionally redundant due to the high degree of sequence and structural similarity, however recent studies have suggested their partially distinct functional roles (Srivastava et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review.

claim: The desensitization, ubiquitination, and endocytosis of β2AR is primarily mediated by β-arrestin 2, not by β-arrestin 1.
source: For example, the desensitization, ubiquitination, and endocytosis of β2AR is primarily mediated by β-arrestin 2, not by β-arrestin 1 (Han et al., 2013; Jean-Charles et al., 2016; Shenoy and Lefkowitz, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: AT1aR-mediated ERK signaling is eliminated by β-arrestin 2 KD in HEK 293 cells, while β-arrestin 1 KD augments ERK signaling.
source: AT1aR-mediated ERK signaling is eliminated by β-arrestin 2 KD in HEK 293 cells, while β-arrestin 1 KD augments ERK signaling (Ahn et al., 2004; Srivastava et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: β-arrestin 1 and 2 exhibit functional redundancy for mGlu7.
source: Our current study showed that β-arrestin 1 and 2 exhibit functional redundancy for mGlu7, while β-arrestin 2 seems to have a lower binding affinity to mGlu7 than β-arrestin 1.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental observations in the current study.

claim: β-arrestin 2 seems to have a lower binding affinity to mGlu7 than β-arrestin 1.
source: Our current study showed that β-arrestin 1 and 2 exhibit functional redundancy for mGlu7, while β-arrestin 2 seems to have a lower binding affinity to mGlu7 than β-arrestin 1.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: Both β-arrestin 1 and 2 are required for constitutive endocytosis of mGlu7 in cultured hippocampal neurons.
source: Both β-arrestin 1 and 2 are required for constitutive endocytosis of mGlu7 in cultured hippocampal neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental observations.

claim: β-arrestin 1 increases agonist-induced ERK signaling in mGlu7 in HEK 293 cells.
source: In contrast, Iacovelli et al. has reported the opposite effect of β-arrestin 1 versus β-arrestin 2 on mGlu7-mediated signaling in HEK 293 cells. They showed that β-arrestin 1 increases or decreases agonist-induced ERK or JNK signaling, respectively, while β-arrestin 2 exerts the opposite effects (Iacovelli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: β-arrestin 1 decreases agonist-induced JNK signaling in mGlu7 in HEK 293 cells.
source: In contrast, Iacovelli et al. has reported the opposite effect of β-arrestin 1 versus β-arrestin 2 on mGlu7-mediated signaling in HEK 293 cells. They showed that β-arrestin 1 increases or decreases agonist-induced ERK or JNK signaling, respectively, while β-arrestin 2 exerts the opposite effects (Iacovelli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The discrepancy in β-arrestin effects on mGlu7 signaling may be caused by the difference in the expression system of primary neurons versus heterologous cells.
source: This discrepancy may be caused by the difference in the expression system of primary neurons versus heterologous cells.
evidence: This is speculation about the reason for discrepant results.

claim: Upon ubiquitination, ligand-stimulated receptors on the plasma membrane are primarily degraded by the lysosome.
source: Upon ubiquitination, ligand-stimulated receptors on the plasma membrane are primarily degraded by the lysosome, whereas most of the ubiquitinated proteins in the cytoplasm are degraded by the proteasome (Foot et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Most of the ubiquitinated proteins in the cytoplasm are degraded by the proteasome.
source: Upon ubiquitination, ligand-stimulated receptors on the plasma membrane are primarily degraded by the lysosome, whereas most of the ubiquitinated proteins in the cytoplasm are degraded by the proteasome (Foot et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Ubiquitinated mGlu7 can be directly translocated to the proteasome.
source: It may be possible that ubiquitinated mGlu7 can be directly translocated to the proteasome or ubiquitinated β-arrestin-Nedd4 can guide mGlu7 as a complex to the proteasome for degradation.
evidence: This is speculation about possible mechanisms.

claim: Ubiquitinated β-arrestin-Nedd4 can guide mGlu7 as a complex to the proteasome for degradation.
source: It may be possible that ubiquitinated mGlu7 can be directly translocated to the proteasome or ubiquitinated β-arrestin-Nedd4 can guide mGlu7 as a complex to the proteasome for degradation.
evidence: This is speculation about possible mechanisms.

claim: Proteasomal activity is required for ligand-induced degradation of multiple receptor types including interleukin-2 receptor, platelet-derived growth factor β receptor, Met tyrosine kinase receptor, epidermal growth factor receptor, growth hormone receptor, TrkA receptor, and AMPA receptor.
source: Similar to our results, it has been reported that proteasomal activity is required for ligand-induced degradation of the interleukin-2 receptor, platelet-derived growth factor β receptor, Met tyrosine kinase receptor, epidermal growth factor receptor, growth hormone receptor, tropomyosin-regulated kinase A (TrkA) receptor, and AMPA receptor (Geetha and Wooten, 2008; Jeffers et al., 1997; Kesarwala et al., 2009; Lin et al., 2011; Lin and Man, 2013; Mori et al., 1995; van Kerkhof et al., 2000; Yu and Malek, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: β-arrestins and Nedd4 play pivotal roles in regulating mGlu7 ubiquitination, endocytosis, signaling, and stability in heterologous cells and neurons.
source: In conclusion, β-arrestins and Nedd4 play pivotal roles in regulating mGlu7 ubiquitination, endocytosis, signaling, and stability in heterologous cells and neurons.
evidence: This is the overall conclusion of the study based on all experimental findings.

claim: These findings will offer novel mechanistic insights for developing selective drugs with therapeutic potentials for mGlu7-related neuropsychiatric disorders.
source: These findings will offer novel mechanistic insights for developing selective drugs with therapeutic potentials for mGlu7-related neuropsychiatric disorders.
evidence: This is speculation about the potential applications of the findings.
